# Codex conversation

## User

# Personal Blog — Coding Agent Instructions

Build a **beautiful, fast, editorial-style personal blog** using Astro.

The priority is:

1. Excellent reading UX
2. Excellent visual design
3. Extremely fast performance
4. Simple content workflow
5. Minimal maintenance
6. Keep the architecture extensible without overengineering

## Stack

Use:

* Astro
* TypeScript
* Tailwind CSS
* MDX
* Astro Content Collections
* Pagefind
* Git/GitHub
* Cloudflare for deployment

Do **not** introduce:

* Rust backend
* PostgreSQL
* Custom CMS
* Authentication
* Custom CLI
* React/Next.js unless there is a specific, demonstrated need

The initial blog should be entirely static-first.

---

# 1. Project setup

Create a clean Astro project with:

* TypeScript strict mode
* Tailwind CSS
* MDX
* ESLint
* Prettier
* Astro Content Collections
* GitHub-ready project
* production build configuration

Keep dependencies minimal.

Prefer Astro components over React components.

Only introduce client-side JavaScript when it materially improves UX.

---

# 2. Project structure

Use a structure approximately like:

```text
src/
├── components/
│   ├── Header.astro
│   ├── Footer.astro
│   ├── PostCard.astro
│   ├── PostHeader.astro
│   ├── TableOfContents.astro
│   ├── CodeBlock.astro
│   ├── Search.astro
│   └── ...
│
├── content/
│   └── posts/
│
├── layouts/
│   ├── BaseLayout.astro
│   └── PostLayout.astro
│
├── pages/
│   ├── index.astro
│   ├── about.astro
│   ├── blog/
│   ├── tags/
│   └── rss.xml.ts
│
├── styles/
│   └── global.css
│
└── content.config.ts
```

Adapt the structure where appropriate, but don't create unnecessary abstractions.

---

# 3. Design direction

Create an **editorial personal blog**, not a SaaS dashboard.

The design should feel:

* sophisticated
* calm
* personal
* typography-focused
* modern
* minimal
* highly readable

Avoid generic startup aesthetics.

Avoid excessive:

* gradients
* cards
* shadows
* rounded containers
* animations
* decorative UI
* JavaScript

Content should be the visual focus.

---

# 4. Typography

Typography is a major design priority.

Establish a deliberate type scale for:

* body
* article body
* headings
* metadata
* navigation
* captions
* code

Article text should have:

* comfortable line length
* generous line height
* strong hierarchy
* excellent spacing between paragraphs
* readable links
* good contrast

Target approximately **65–75 characters per line** for article prose.

Use optimized/local fonts where practical and avoid unnecessary font requests.

---

# 5. Theme

Implement light and dark themes.

Requirements:

* respect system preference initially
* allow manual switching
* persist user preference
* avoid flash of incorrect theme
* accessible contrast

Use semantic color tokens rather than hardcoding colors throughout components.

---

# 6. Navigation

Desktop navigation should be minimal.

Example:

```text
Name        Blog   About   Search   Theme
```

Mobile navigation should remain simple and fast.

Do not build a complicated hamburger system unless necessary.

Keyboard navigation must work correctly.

---

# 7. Homepage

Create a distinctive personal homepage.

Include:

* short personal introduction
* selected/recent posts
* topics/tags
* optional featured article
* simple about section
* RSS/social links

Do not overcrowd the homepage.

The page should communicate personality without becoming visually noisy.

---

# 8. Blog index

Create:

```text
/blog
```

Include:

* article list
* title
* short description
* date
* tags
* reading time where useful

Use clean editorial layouts rather than card grids by default.

If there are many posts, support pagination or another appropriate navigation strategy.

---

# 9. Article pages

Create:

```text
/blog/[slug]
```

Each article should support:

* title
* description
* published date
* updated date
* tags
* reading time
* optional hero image
* article body
* table of contents for long articles
* related posts
* previous/next navigation

The article page should be the highest-quality page in the application.

---

# 10. Content schema

Use Astro Content Collections.

Post frontmatter should support:

```yaml
---
title: "Example Post"
description: "Short description"
date: 2026-09-29
updated: 2026-09-29
tags:
  - programming
  - rust
draft: false
image:
---
```

Use schema validation.

Do not make content dependent on a database.

Markdown/MDX files are the source of truth.

---

# 11. MDX components

Support a small set of useful components where appropriate:

```text
Callout
Figure
Image
Quote
YouTube
Code
```

Do not create components merely for the sake of abstraction.

Content must remain portable and understandable as Markdown/MDX.

---

# 12. Code blocks

Technical articles should have excellent code presentation.

Support:

* syntax highlighting
* horizontal scrolling on mobile
* copy button
* language labels where useful
* accessible controls

Avoid shipping a large client-side code editor.

---

# 13. Images

Use Astro's image tooling.

Requirements:

* responsive images
* optimized formats
* explicit dimensions
* lazy loading below the fold
* eager/priority loading for important hero images
* meaningful alt text
* avoid layout shifts

Never serve unnecessarily large source images.

---

# 14. Search

Add Pagefind after the basic blog works.

Search should:

* search titles
* search article content
* search tags
* return results quickly
* work well on mobile

Add a keyboard shortcut:

```text
Cmd/Ctrl + K
```

for opening search if this can be done cleanly.

Search should not require a backend.

---

# 15. Motion

Use subtle motion only.

Prefer:

* CSS transitions
* CSS transforms
* Astro View Transitions where appropriate

Respect:

```text
prefers-reduced-motion
```

Never sacrifice performance for animation.

---

# 16. SEO

Implement:

* semantic HTML
* unique title tags
* meta descriptions
* canonical URLs
* Open Graph metadata
* social preview images where appropriate
* sitemap
* robots.txt
* RSS
* Article structured data
* clean URLs

Example:

```text
/blog/building-a-personal-blog
```

Avoid unnecessary query-based URLs.

---

# 17. Accessibility

Target WCAG 2.2 AA.

Ensure:

* keyboard navigation
* visible focus states
* semantic landmarks
* correct heading hierarchy
* accessible buttons
* accessible forms
* sufficient contrast
* useful alt text
* reduced-motion support
* mobile accessibility

Do not rely on hover-only interactions.

---

# 18. Performance

Treat performance as a core feature.

Target:

```text
LCP < 2.5s
CLS < 0.1
INP < 200ms
```

Use:

* Astro static generation
* minimal JavaScript
* optimized images
* optimized fonts
* minimal dependencies
* CSS instead of JS where possible
* CDN caching

Do not add libraries without a concrete reason.

---

# 19. CLI/content workflow

Do not build a custom CLI yet.

Provide a simple npm script for creating posts:

```bash
npm run new -- "My New Post"
```

This should create a correctly named MDX file with appropriate frontmatter.

Normal workflow should be:

```bash
npm run new -- "My New Post"
npm run dev
npm run build
git add .
git commit
git push
```

Keep Markdown files directly editable through any editor.

---

# 20. Deployment

Deploy through GitHub → Cloudflare.

Desired workflow:

```text
git push
   ↓
GitHub
   ↓
CI
   ↓
Astro build
   ↓
Cloudflare deployment
```

Production should deploy automatically from `main`.

Pull requests should use preview deployments if supported.

---

# 21. Testing

Implement lightweight but meaningful testing.

CI should run:

```text
Type checking
Lint
Formatting check
Astro build
```

Add Playwright for critical user flows where useful.

Manually verify:

* mobile
* tablet
* desktop
* dark mode
* keyboard navigation
* long articles
* code-heavy articles
* slow network
* reduced motion

---

# 22. Analytics

Do not add analytics until the core experience works.

If analytics are added, prefer a lightweight solution.

Track only useful events such as:

* page views
* article engagement
* outbound links
* search usage

Avoid unnecessary tracking scripts.

---

# 23. Engineering principles

Follow these principles throughout implementation:

### Prefer simplicity

Do not solve hypothetical future problems.

### Static first

If something can be generated at build time, generate it at build time.

### Minimal JavaScript

Every client-side dependency should have a clear UX justification.

### Content ownership

Markdown/MDX remains the canonical content source.

### Progressive enhancement

The site should remain useful without JavaScript wherever practical.

### Accessibility is part of implementation

Do not treat accessibility as a final checklist.

### Performance is part of design

Do not add visual features that substantially harm performance.

### Avoid premature abstraction

Build concrete components first. Abstract only when repetition is real.

---

# 24. Future extensibility

Do not implement these now:

```text
Rust API
PostgreSQL
Browser CMS
Authentication
Custom Rust CLI
```

However, structure the code so these can be introduced later without redesigning the public site.

Potential future architecture:

```text
                 Astro
                   │
             Static website
                   │
          ┌────────┴────────┐
          │                 │
       Markdown         Rust API
                            │
                       PostgreSQL
```

Do not build this architecture until there is an actual requirement.

---

# 25. Definition of done

The first release is complete when:

* The site looks intentionally designed rather than template-generated.
* Reading an article feels excellent on both desktop and mobile.
* Blog content is easy to create/edit through Markdown.
* Dark/light mode works correctly.
* Search works.
* RSS works.
* SEO metadata and sitemap work.
* Images are optimized.
* Keyboard navigation works.
* Core pages are accessible.
* JavaScript usage is minimal.
* Production builds successfully.
* Cloudflare deployment works.
* Lighthouse and real-world performance are strong.

## Final principle

Build **the smallest system capable of producing an exceptionally good personal blog**.

Do not build a CMS, backend, database, or platform just because the architecture might eventually need one.

The product is the **blog and reading experience**, not the infrastructure.

    ---
    
    There is something useful about having a place to think in public without having to perform for a feed.
    
    This blog is an ongoing collection of notes about making things with care. Some will be practical. Some will be unfinished. The common thread is attention: to the tools we choose, the systems we build, and the quality of the ordinary decisions in between.
    
    ## A slower publishing rhythm
    
    I want these pages to feel more like a desk drawer than a content machine. A few good notes are enough. If something here helps you make a better decision or notice something you had been rushing past, it has done its job.
    
    Thanks for reading.

## Assistant

The project is already scaffolded, but it is very compressed and incomplete: the article route lacks the requested reading features, search is only a placeholder, tags are missing, and several files contain mojibake characters. I’m going to turn that into a coherent editorial system with reusable layout primitives, static tag pages, Pagefind-powered search, RSS/SEO plumbing, and a safer theme toggle.

The first edit batch hit a context mismatch caused by the existing malformed characters, so it did not change the repository. I’m switching to smaller file-level patches to avoid disturbing unrelated content and keep the edits auditable.

## Activity

    file changes: Completed · 1 changes
    Add: D:\freemodels\pers-blog\src\pages\search.astro
    ---
    import BaseLayout from '../layouts/BaseLayout.astro';
    ---
    <BaseLayout title="Search">
      <section class="mx-auto max-w-3xl px-6 pb-20 pt-16 lg:pt-24">
        <p class="mono text-xs uppercase tracking-[.2em] text-[var(--accent)]">Find a note</p>
        <h1 class="serif mt-5 text-6xl tracking-tight">Search</h1>
        <div id="search" class="mt-12"></div>
      </section>
      <script type="module">
        const root = document.querySelector('#search');
        if (root) {
          const { default: pagefind } = await import('/pagefind/pagefind.js');
          const input = document.createElement('input');
          input.type = 'search';
          input.placeholder = 'Search the archive';
          input.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Search the archive');
          input.className = 'w-full border-b border-[var(--line)] bg-transparent px-0 py-4 text-xl outline-none';
          root.append(input);
          const results = document.createElement('div');
          results.className = 'mt-8 space-y-6';
          root.append(results);
          input.addEventListener('input', async () => {
            results.replaceChildren();
            if (!input.value) return;
            const data = await pagefind.search(input.value);
            for (const item of data.results.slice(0, 8)) {
              const result = await item.data();
              const link = document.createElement('a');
              link.href = result.url;
              link.className = 'block border-t border-[var(--line)] pt-4';
              link.innerHTML = `<strong>${result.meta.title ?? 'Untitled'}</strong><p class="mt-1 text-sm text-[var(--muted)]">${result.excerpt ?? ''}</p>`;
              results.append(link);
            }
          });
          window.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
            if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === 'k') {
              event.preventDefault();
              input.focus();
            }
          });
        }
      </script>
    </BaseLayout>

    Add: D:\freemodels\pers-blog\README.md
    # Field Notes
    
    Field Notes is a static-first personal blog built with Astro. Posts live as Markdown or MDX files in the repository; Astro generates the pages, and Pagefind builds a local search index as part of the production build.
    
    ## Requirements
    
    - Node.js 22.12 or later
    - npm
    
    ## Get started
    
    ```sh
    npm install
    npm run dev
    ```
    
    Astro prints the local development URL when the server starts (usually `http://localhost:4321`). The repository's `AGENTS.md` asks agents to start the development server in the background with `astro dev --background`; use `astro dev status`, `astro dev logs`, and `astro dev stop` to manage it.
    
    ## Write a post
    
    Create a draft with the post generator:
    
    ```sh
    npm run new -- "A useful note"
    ```
    
    This creates `src/content/posts/a-useful-note.mdx` with starter frontmatter. Edit the file directly and set `draft: false` when it is ready to publish. Posts marked as drafts are omitted from the public pages, RSS feed, tag pages, and search index.
    
    Example frontmatter:
    
    ```yaml
    ---
    title: "A useful note"
    description: "A short summary for the archive and search results."
    date: 2026-09-29
    updated: 2026-09-30
    tags:
      - craft
      - web
    draft: false
    ---
    ```
    
    The `updated` date is optional. `tags` defaults to an empty list. The collection schema in `src/content.config.ts` validates post metadata during development and builds. Article URLs use the filename as a slug, without the `.md` or `.mdx` extension.
    
    ## Project structure
    
    ```text
    src/
    ├── components/       Shared page elements, including the blog sidebar
    ├── content/posts/    Markdown and MDX posts
    ├── layouts/          Shared site layout and document metadata
    ├── lib/              Post queries, dates, and URL helpers
    ├── pages/            Homepage, archive, articles, tags, search, and RSS
    ├── styles/           Global design tokens and typography
    └── content.config.ts Content collection schema
    public/               Static files served as-is
    scripts/              Small post creation script
    ```
    
    ## Commands
    
    | Command | Purpose |
    | --- | --- |
    | `npm run dev` | Start Astro's local development server |
    | `npm run check` | Check Astro and TypeScript diagnostics |
    | `npm run lint` | Run ESLint |
    | `npm run format` | Check formatting with Prettier |
    | `npm run build` | Build the static site, then index `dist/` with Pagefind |
    | `npm run preview` | Preview the production build locally |
    | `npm run new -- "Post title"` | Create a draft MDX post |
    
    Run `npm run build` before previewing. Pagefind indexes the generated HTML under `dist/pagefind`; the search page loads that index from the same deployed site. The production build also generates the sitemap. RSS is available at `/rss.xml`.
    
    ## Configuration
    
    Set the production site URL in `astro.config.mjs` before deploying. The current value is a placeholder (`https://fieldnotes.example`); use the canonical domain so canonical links and the sitemap point to the right host.
    
    The global theme styles and color tokens are in `src/styles/global.css`. The theme toggle stores the reader's selection in local storage and otherwise follows their system preference.
    
    ## Deploy
    
    The site is configured for static output. Build with `npm run build` and deploy the contents of `dist/` to a static host such as Cloudflare Pages. Configure the host to build from the GitHub repository with:
    
    - Build command: `npm run build`
    - Build output directory: `dist`
    - Node.js: 22.12 or later
    
    Pushes to the production branch can trigger production builds; pull requests can use the host's preview deployments. No server, database, or environment variables are required for the current site.
    
    ## Further reading
    
    - [Astro documentation](https://docs.astro.build/)
    - [Astro content collections](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/content-collections/)
    - [Pagefind documentation](https://pagefind.app/docs/)

    ---
    <BaseLayout title="Search">
      <section class="mx-auto max-w-3xl px-6 pb-20 pt-16 lg:pt-24">
        <p class="mono text-xs uppercase tracking-[.2em] text-[var(--accent)]">Find a note</p>
        <h1 class="serif mt-5 text-6xl tracking-tight">Search</h1>
        <div id="search" class="mt-12"></div>
      </section>
      <script type="module">
        const root = document.querySelector('#search');
        if (root) {
          const { default: pagefind } = await import('/pagefind/pagefind.js');
          const input = document.createElement('input');
          input.type = 'search';
          input.placeholder = 'Search the archive';
          input.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Search the archive');
          input.className = 'w-full border-b border-[var(--line)] bg-transparent px-0 py-4 text-xl outline-none';
          root.append(input);
          const results = document.createElement('div');
          results.className = 'mt-8 space-y-6';
          root.append(results);
          input.addEventListener('input', async () => {
            results.replaceChildren();
            if (!input.value) return;
            const data = await pagefind.search(input.value);
            for (const item of data.results.slice(0, 8)) {
              const result = await item.data();
              const link = document.createElement('a');
              link.href = result.url;
              link.className = 'block border-t border-[var(--line)] pt-4';
              link.innerHTML = `<strong>${result.meta.title ?? 'Untitled'}</strong><p class="mt-1 text-sm text-[var(--muted)]">${result.excerpt ?? ''}</p>`;
              results.append(link);
            }
          });
          window.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
            if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === 'k') {
              event.preventDefault();
              input.focus();
            }
          });
        }
      </script>
    </BaseLayout>

    # Field Notes
    
    Field Notes is a static-first personal blog built with Astro. Posts live as Markdown or MDX files in the repository; Astro generates the pages, and Pagefind builds a local search index as part of the production build.
    
    ## Requirements
    
    - Node.js 22.12 or later
    - npm
    
    ## Get started
    
    ```sh
    npm install
    npm run dev
    ```
    
    Astro prints the local development URL when the server starts (usually `http://localhost:4321`). The repository's `AGENTS.md` asks agents to start the development server in the background with `astro dev --background`; use `astro dev status`, `astro dev logs`, and `astro dev stop` to manage it.
    
    ## Write a post
    
    Create a draft with the post generator:
    
    ```sh
    npm run new -- "A useful note"
    ```
    
    This creates `src/content/posts/a-useful-note.mdx` with starter frontmatter. Edit the file directly and set `draft: false` when it is ready to publish. Posts marked as drafts are omitted from the public pages, RSS feed, tag pages, and search index.
    
    Example frontmatter:
    
    ```yaml
    ---
    title: "A useful note"
    description: "A short summary for the archive and search results."
    date: 2026-09-29
    updated: 2026-09-30
    tags:
      - craft
      - web
    draft: false
    ---
    ```
    
    The `updated` date is optional. `tags` defaults to an empty list. The collection schema in `src/content.config.ts` validates post metadata during development and builds. Article URLs use the filename as a slug, without the `.md` or `.mdx` extension.
    
    ## Project structure
    
    ```text
    src/
    â”œâ”€â”€ components/       Shared page elements, including the blog sidebar
    â”œâ”€â”€ content/posts/    Markdown and MDX posts
    â”œâ”€â”€ layouts/          Shared site layout and document metadata
    â”œâ”€â”€ lib/              Post queries, dates, and URL helpers
    â”œâ”€â”€ pages/            Homepage, archive, articles, tags, search, and RSS
    â”œâ”€â”€ styles/           Global design tokens and typography
    â””â”€â”€ content.config.ts Content collection schema
    public/               Static files served as-is
    scripts/              Small post creation script
    ```
    
    ## Commands
    
    | Command | Purpose |
    | --- | --- |
    | `npm run dev` | Start Astro's local development server |
    | `npm run check` | Check Astro and TypeScript diagnostics |
    | `npm run lint` | Run ESLint |
    | `npm run format` | Check formatting with Prettier |
    | `npm run build` | Build the static site, then index `dist/` with Pagefind |
    | `npm run preview` | Preview the production build locally |
    | `npm run new -- "Post title"` | Create a draft MDX post |
    
    Run `npm run build` before previewing. Pagefind indexes the generated HTML under `dist/pagefind`; the search page loads that index from the same deployed site. The production build also generates the sitemap. RSS is available at `/rss.xml`.
    
    ## Configuration
    
    Set the production site URL in `astro.config.mjs` before deploying. The current value is a placeholder (`https://fieldnotes.example`); use the canonical domain so canonical links and the sitemap point to the right host.
    
    The global theme styles and color tokens are in `src/styles/global.css`. The theme toggle stores the reader's selection in local storage and otherwise follows their system preference.
    
    ## Deploy
    
    The site is configured for static output. Build with `npm run build` and deploy the contents of `dist/` to a static host such as Cloudflare Pages. Configure the host to build from the GitHub repository with:
    
    - Build command: `npm run build`
    - Build output directory: `dist`
    - Node.js: 22.12 or later
    
    Pushes to the production branch can trigger production builds; pull requests can use the host's preview deployments. No server, database, or environment variables are required for the current site.
    
    ## Further reading
    
    - [Astro documentation](https://docs.astro.build/)
    - [Astro content collections](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/content-collections/)
    - [Pagefind documentation](https://pagefind.app/docs/)

    ---
    import BaseLayout from '../layouts/BaseLayout.astro';
    ---
    <BaseLayout title="Search">
      <section class="mx-auto max-w-3xl px-6 pb-20 pt-16 lg:pt-24">
        <p class="mono text-xs uppercase tracking-[.2em] text-[var(--accent)]">Find a note</p>
        <h1 class="serif mt-5 text-6xl tracking-tight">Search</h1>
        <div id="search" class="mt-12"></div>
      </section>
      <script type="module">
        const root = document.querySelector('#search');
        if (root) {
          const { default: pagefind } = await import('/pagefind/pagefind.js');
          const input = document.createElement('input');
          input.type = 'search';
          input.placeholder = 'Search the archive';
          input.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Search the archive');
          input.className = 'w-full border-b border-[var(--line)] bg-transparent px-0 py-4 text-xl outline-none';
          root.append(input);
          const results = document.createElement('div');
          results.className = 'mt-8 space-y-6';
          root.append(results);
          input.addEventListener('input', async () => {
            results.replaceChildren();
            if (!input.value) return;
            const data = await pagefind.search(input.value);
            for (const item of data.results.slice(0, 8)) {
              const result = await item.data();
              const link = document.createElement('a');
              link.href = result.url;
              link.className = 'block border-t border-[var(--line)] pt-4';
              link.innerHTML = `<strong>${result.meta.title ?? 'Untitled'}</strong><p class="mt-1 text-sm text-[var(--muted)]">${result.excerpt ?? ''}</p>`;
              results.append(link);
            }
          });
          window.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
            if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === 'k') {
              event.preventDefault();
              input.focus();
            }
          });
        }
      </script>
    </BaseLayout>

    ---
    import BaseLayout from '../layouts/BaseLayout.astro';
    ---
    <BaseLayout title="Search">
      <section class="shell max-w-3xl pb-20 pt-16 lg:pt-24">
        <p class="mono text-xs uppercase tracking-[.2em] text-[var(--accent)]">The archive</p>
        <h1 class="serif mt-5 text-6xl tracking-tight">Search</h1>
        <label class="sr-only" for="site-search">Search posts</label>
        <input id="site-search" class="search-input mt-10" type="search" placeholder="Search posts…" autocomplete="off" />
        <p id="search-status" class="search-status mt-5" role="status" aria-live="polite">Search titles and posts by keyword.</p>
        <div id="search-results" class="mt-6" aria-label="Search results"></div>
      </section>
      <script>
        const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('#site-search');
        const output = document.querySelector<HTMLDivElement>('#search-results');
        const status = document.querySelector<HTMLParagraphElement>('#search-status');
        let pagefind: { search: (query: string) => Promise<{ results: Array<{ data: () => Promise<{ url: string; meta: { title?: string }; excerpt: string }> }> }> } | undefined;
        let timer: number | undefined;
    
        async function getPagefind() {
          if (pagefind) return pagefind;
          const basePath = import.meta.env.BASE_URL;
          const moduleUrl = `${basePath.replace(/\/$/, '')}/pagefind/pagefind.js`;
          const module = await import(/* @vite-ignore */ moduleUrl);
          pagefind = module.default;
          return pagefind;
        }
    
        input?.addEventListener('input', () => {
          window.clearTimeout(timer);
          timer = window.setTimeout(async () => {
            const query = input.value.trim();
            if (!output || !status) return;
            output.replaceChildren();
            if (!query) {
              status.textContent = 'Search titles and posts by keyword.';
              return;
            }
    
            status.textContent = 'Searching…';
            try {
              const search = await getPagefind();
              const response = await search.search(query);
              const results = await Promise.all(response.results.slice(0, 10).map((item) => item.data()));
              status.textContent = results.length ? `${results.length}${response.results.length > 10 ? '+' : ''} results` : 'No matching posts.';
              for (const result of results) {
                const link = document.createElement('a');
                link.href = result.url;
                link.className = 'search-result';
                const title = document.createElement('span');
                title.className = 'search-result-title';
                title.textContent = result.meta.title ?? 'Untitled';
                const excerpt = document.createElement('p');
                excerpt.className = 'search-result-excerpt';
                excerpt.textContent = result.excerpt.replace(/<[^>]*>/g, '');
                link.append(title, excerpt);
                output.append(link);
              }
            } catch {
              status.textContent = 'Search is available after a production build. Try `npm run build`, then preview the site.';
            }
          }, 120);
        });
    
        window.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
          if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === 'k') {
            event.preventDefault();
            input?.focus();
          }
        });
      </script>
    </BaseLayout>

Updated the design with a near-black default theme, warm text, lime accents, quieter dividers, and cleaner archive styling. The theme toggle still lets readers switch to light mode.

I also found a likely search issue: Pagefind’s index is generated during production builds, so it isn’t available from the regular Astro dev server. Search now shows a clear message when that index is missing, debounces queries, and safely displays results when it is available.

    # Field Notes
    
    Field Notes is a static-first personal blog built with Astro. Posts live as Markdown or MDX files in the repository; Astro generates the pages, and Pagefind builds a local search index as part of the production build.
    
    ## Requirements
    
    - Node.js 22.12 or later
    - npm
    
    ## Get started
    
    ```sh
    npm install
    npm run dev
    ```
    
    Astro prints the local development URL when the server starts (usually `http://localhost:4321`). The repository's `AGENTS.md` asks agents to start the development server in the background with `astro dev --background`; use `astro dev status`, `astro dev logs`, and `astro dev stop` to manage it.
    
    ## Write a post
    
    Create a draft with the post generator:
    
    ```sh
    npm run new -- "A useful note"
    ```
    
    This creates `src/content/posts/a-useful-note.mdx` with starter frontmatter. Edit the file directly and set `draft: false` when it is ready to publish. Posts marked as drafts are omitted from the public pages, RSS feed, tag pages, and search index.
    
    Example frontmatter:
    
    ```yaml
    ---
    title: "A useful note"
    description: "A short summary for the archive and search results."
    date: 2026-09-29
    updated: 2026-09-30
    tags:
      - craft
      - web
    draft: false
    ---
    ```
    
    The `updated` date is optional. `tags` defaults to an empty list. The collection schema in `src/content.config.ts` validates post metadata during development and builds. Article URLs use the filename as a slug, without the `.md` or `.mdx` extension.
    
    ## Project structure
    
    ```text
    src/
    â”œâ”€â”€ components/       Shared page elements, including the blog sidebar
    â”œâ”€â”€ content/posts/    Markdown and MDX posts
    â”œâ”€â”€ layouts/          Shared site layout and document metadata
    â”œâ”€â”€ lib/              Post queries, dates, and URL helpers
    â”œâ”€â”€ pages/            Homepage, archive, articles, tags, search, and RSS
    â”œâ”€â”€ styles/           Global design tokens and typography
    â””â”€â”€ content.config.ts Content collection schema
    public/               Static files served as-is
    scripts/              Small post creation script
    ```
    
    ## Commands
    
    | Command | Purpose |
    | --- | --- |
    | `npm run dev` | Start Astro's local development server |
    | `npm run check` | Check Astro and TypeScript diagnostics |
    | `npm run lint` | Run ESLint |
    | `npm run format` | Check formatting with Prettier |
    | `npm run build` | Build the static site, then index `dist/` with Pagefind |
    | `npm run preview` | Preview the production build locally |
    | `npm run new -- "Post title"` | Create a draft MDX post |
    
    Run `npm run build` before previewing. Pagefind indexes the generated HTML under `dist/pagefind`; the search page loads that index from the same deployed site. The production build also generates the sitemap. RSS is available at `/rss.xml`.
    
    ## Configuration
    
    Set the production site URL in `astro.config.mjs` before deploying. The current value is a placeholder (`https://fieldnotes.example`); use the canonical domain so canonical links and the sitemap point to the right host.
    
    The global theme styles and color tokens are in `src/styles/global.css`. The theme toggle stores the reader's selection in local storage and otherwise follows their system preference.
    
    ## Deploy
    
    The site is configured for static output. Build with `npm run build` and deploy the contents of `dist/` to a static host such as Cloudflare Pages. Configure the host to build from the GitHub repository with:
    
    - Build command: `npm run build`
    - Build output directory: `dist`
    - Node.js: 22.12 or later
    
    Pushes to the production branch can trigger production builds; pull requests can use the host's preview deployments. No server, database, or environment variables are required for the current site.
    
    ## Further reading
    
    - [Astro documentation](https://docs.astro.build/)
    - [Astro content collections](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/content-collections/)
    - [Pagefind documentation](https://pagefind.app/docs/)

    title: "Welcome to Field Notes"
    description: "Why this small corner of the internet exists, and what I hope to put here."
    date: 2026-09-29
    tags:
      - life
      - craft
    draft: false
    ---
    
    There is something useful about having a place to think in public without having to perform for a feed.
    
    This blog is an ongoing collection of notes about making things with care. Some will be practical. Some will be unfinished. The common thread is attention: to the tools we choose, the systems we build, and the quality of the ordinary decisions in between.
    
    ## A slower publishing rhythm
    
    I want these pages to feel more like a desk drawer than a content machine. A few good notes are enough. If something here helps you make a better decision or notice something you had been rushing past, it has done its job.
    
    Thanks for reading.

    import { defineCollection, z } from 'astro:content';
    
    const sharedFields = {
      title: z.string(),
      description: z.string(),
      date: z.coerce.date(),
      draft: z.boolean().default(false),
    };
    
    const posts = defineCollection({
      type: 'content',
      schema: z.object({
        ...sharedFields,
        updated: z.coerce.date().optional(),
        tags: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
        image: z.string().optional(),
      }),
    });
    
    const projects = defineCollection({
      type: 'content',
      schema: z.object({
        ...sharedFields,
        status: z.enum(['active', 'complete', 'archived']).default('complete'),
        url: z.string().url().optional(),
        repository: z.string().url().optional(),
        tags: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
        image: z.string().optional(),
      }),
    });
    
    const links = defineCollection({

    # Field Notes
    
    Field Notes is a static-first personal blog built with Astro. Posts live as Markdown or MDX files in the repository; Astro generates the pages, and Pagefind builds a local search index as part of the production build.
    
    ## Requirements
    
    - Node.js 22.12 or later
    - npm
    
    ## Get started
    
    ```sh
    npm install
    npm run dev
    ```
    
    Astro prints the local development URL when the server starts (usually `http://localhost:4321`). The repository's `AGENTS.md` asks agents to start the development server in the background with `astro dev --background`; use `astro dev status`, `astro dev logs`, and `astro dev stop` to manage it.
    
    ## Write a post
    
    Create a draft with the post generator:
    
    ```sh
    npm run new -- "A useful note"
    ```
    
    This creates `src/content/posts/a-useful-note.mdx` with starter frontmatter. Edit the file directly and set `draft: false` when it is ready to publish. Posts marked as drafts are omitted from the public pages, RSS feed, tag pages, and search index.
    
    Example frontmatter:
    
    ```yaml
    ---
    title: "A useful note"
    description: "A short summary for the archive and search results."
    date: 2026-09-29
    updated: 2026-09-30
    tags:
      - craft
      - web
    draft: false
    ---
    ```
    
    The `updated` date is optional. `tags` defaults to an empty list. The collection schema in `src/content.config.ts` validates post metadata during development and builds. Article URLs use the filename as a slug, without the `.md` or `.mdx` extension.
    
    ## Project structure
    
    ```text
    src/
    ├── components/       Shared page elements, including the blog sidebar
    ├── content/posts/    Markdown and MDX posts
    ├── layouts/          Shared site layout and document metadata
    ├── lib/              Post queries, dates, and URL helpers
    ├── pages/            Homepage, archive, articles, tags, search, and RSS
    ├── styles/           Global design tokens and typography
    └── content.config.ts Content collection schema
    public/               Static files served as-is
    scripts/              Small post creation script
    ```
    
    ## Commands
    
    | Command | Purpose |
    | --- | --- |
    | `npm run dev` | Start Astro's local development server |
    | `npm run check` | Check Astro and TypeScript diagnostics |
    | `npm run lint` | Run ESLint |
    | `npm run format` | Check formatting with Prettier |
    | `npm run build` | Build the static site, then index `dist/` with Pagefind |
    | `npm run preview` | Preview the production build locally |
    | `npm run new -- "Post title"` | Create a draft MDX post |
    
    Run `npm run build` before previewing. Pagefind indexes the generated HTML under `dist/pagefind`; the search page loads that index from the same deployed site. The production build also generates the sitemap. RSS is available at `/rss.xml`.
    
    ## Configuration
    
    Set the production site URL in `astro.config.mjs` before deploying. The current value is a placeholder (`https://fieldnotes.example`); use the canonical domain so canonical links and the sitemap point to the right host.
    
    The global theme styles and color tokens are in `src/styles/global.css`. The theme toggle stores the reader's selection in local storage and otherwise follows their system preference.
    
    ## Deploy
    
    The site is configured for static output. Build with `npm run build` and deploy the contents of `dist/` to a static host such as Cloudflare Pages. Configure the host to build from the GitHub repository with:
    
    - Build command: `npm run build`
    - Build output directory: `dist`

    # Field Notes
    
    Field Notes is a static personal site built with Astro. Writing, projects, and saved links are Markdown or MDX files in the repository. Astro generates the pages, and Pagefind creates the search index during production builds.
    
    ## Requirements and setup
    
    - Node.js 22.12 or later
    - npm
    
    ```sh
    npm install
    npm run dev
    ```
    
    Astro prints the local development URL (usually `http://localhost:4321`). Search needs the generated Pagefind index, so test it with `npm run build` followed by `npm run preview`.
    
    ## Content
    
    ### Writing
    
    Create a draft article with:
    
    ```sh
    npm run new -- "A useful note"
    ```
    
    This creates `src/content/posts/a-useful-note.mdx`. Edit the file directly and set `draft: false` when ready. The article filename becomes its URL slug. Published articles support `title`, `description`, `date`, optional `updated`, `tags`, `draft`, and optional `image` fields.
    
    ### Projects
    
    Add a Markdown or MDX file under `src/content/projects/`. The filename determines the project detail URL under `/projects/`.
    
    ```yaml
    ---
    title: "A small project"
    description: "What it does and why it exists."
    date: 2026-09-29
    draft: false
    status: active
    url: https://example.org/project
    repository: https://github.com/example/project
    tags:
      - tools
    ---
    
    Describe the project, the process, or what you learned.
    ```
    
    `status` may be `active`, `complete`, or `archived`. `url`, `repository`, and tags are optional. The project appears in the `/projects` index and gets a static detail page.
    
    ### Links
    
    Add a Markdown or MDX file under `src/content/links/`. Each published file adds a curated link to `/links`; it does not create a separate detail page.
    
    ```yaml
    ---
    title: "An article worth saving"
    description: "A note on what makes this useful."
    date: 2026-09-29
    draft: false
    url: https://example.org/article
    source: Example publication
    tags:
      - reading
    ---
    ```
    
    The `url` field is required. `source` and tags are optional. Both Projects and Links support `draft: true` while preparing entries; drafts are excluded from the published pages.
    
    ## Project structure
    
    ```text
    src/
    |-- components/       Shared site components
    |-- content/
    |   |-- posts/        Articles
    |   |-- projects/     Project entries
    |   `-- links/        Curated external links
    |-- layouts/          Shared document layout and metadata
    |-- lib/              Post query and URL helpers
    |-- pages/            Static routes and collection pages
    |-- styles/           Theme, typography, and layout styles
    `-- content.config.ts Validated collection schemas
    public/               Static files served as-is
    scripts/              Post creation helper
    ```
    
    ## Commands
    
    | Command | Purpose |
    | --- | --- |
    | `npm run dev` | Start Astro's local development server |
    | `npm run check` | Check Astro and TypeScript diagnostics |
    | `npm run lint` | Run ESLint |
    | `npm run format` | Check formatting with Prettier |
    | `npm run build` | Generate the static site and Pagefind index |
    | `npm run preview` | Preview the production build |
    | `npm run new -- "Post title"` | Create a draft MDX article |
    
    The build generates the sitemap and search index. RSS is available at `/rss.xml`. The header links to Writing, Projects, Links, and Search.
    
    ## Appearance
    
    The dark theme uses a warm charcoal base (`#171916`) with a faint olive-tinted glow, soft gray dividers, and a restrained lime accent. This keeps the page dark without the harsh contrast of pure black and makes the reading surface feel less flat. Readers can switch to the light theme with the header control. Theme tokens and page styling are in `src/styles/global.css`.
    
    ## Configuration and deployment
    
    Update the placeholder `site` URL in `astro.config.mjs` to the production domain. This value is used for canonical URLs, the sitemap, and RSS.
    
    Deploy the static output to Cloudflare Pages:
    
    - Build command: `npm run build`
    - Output directory: `dist`
    - Node.js: 22.12 or later
    
    No backend, database, or environment variables are needed for the current site. GitHub pushes can trigger production builds, with pull request previews enabled in the Pages project settings.

    });

    file changes: Completed · 1 changes
    Add: D:\freemodels\pers-blog\src\layouts\BaseLayout.astro
    ---
    import '../styles/global.css';
    import Header from '../components/Header.astro';
    import Footer from '../components/Footer.astro';
    
    const {
      title = 'Field Notes',
      description = 'A personal blog about making things with care.',
      image,
    } = Astro.props;
    const canonical = new URL(Astro.url.pathname, Astro.site ?? Astro.url.origin);
    ---
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8" />
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width" />
        <link rel="canonical" href={canonical} />
        <meta name="description" content={description} />
        <meta property="og:type" content="article" />
        <meta property="og:title" content={title} />
        <meta property="og:description" content={description} />
        {image && <meta property="og:image" content={new URL(image, Astro.site ?? Astro.url.origin)} />}
        <meta name="theme-color" content="#171916" />
        <title>{title} | Field Notes</title>
        <script is:inline>
          try {
            const theme = localStorage.getItem('theme');
            document.documentElement.dataset.theme = theme === 'light' ? 'light' : 'dark';
          } catch {
            document.documentElement.dataset.theme = 'dark';
          }
        </script>
      </head>
      <body>
        <Header />
        <main><slot /></main>
        <Footer />
        <script is:inline>
          document.getElementById('theme-toggle')?.addEventListener('click', () => {
            const root = document.documentElement;
            const theme = root.dataset.theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark';
            root.dataset.theme = theme;
            try {
              localStorage.setItem('theme', theme);
            } catch {}
          });
        </script>
      </body>
    </html>

    <header class="site-header">
      <div class="shell header-inner">
        <a class="brand serif" href="/" aria-label="Field Notes home">Field Notes<span>.</span></a>
        <nav aria-label="Main navigation" class="main-nav">
          <a href="/blog">Writing</a>
          <a href="/projects">Projects</a>
          <a href="/links">Links</a>
          <a href="/search">Search</a>
          <button id="theme-toggle" class="theme-toggle" type="button" aria-label="Switch to light theme" title="Switch theme">Aa</button>
        </nav>
      </div>
    </header>
    ---
    import BaseLayout from '../layouts/BaseLayout.astro';
    ---
    <BaseLayout title="Search">
      <section class="shell max-w-3xl pb-20 pt-16 lg:pt-24">
        <p class="mono text-xs uppercase tracking-[.2em] text-[var(--muted)]">Search posts</p>
        <h1 class="serif mt-5 text-6xl tracking-tight">Search</h1>
        <label class="sr-only" for="site-search">Search posts</label>
        <input id="site-search" class="search-input mt-10" type="search" placeholder="Search postsâ€¦" autocomplete="off" />
        <p id="search-status" class="search-status mt-5" role="status" aria-live="polite">Search titles and posts by keyword.</p>
        <div id="search-results" class="mt-6" aria-label="Search results"></div>
      </section>
      <script>
        const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('#site-search');
        const output = document.querySelector<HTMLDivElement>('#search-results');
        const status = document.querySelector<HTMLParagraphElement>('#search-status');
        let pagefind: { search: (query: string) => Promise<{ results: Array<{ data: () => Promise<{ url: string; meta: { title?: string }; excerpt: string }> }> }> } | undefined;
        let timer: number | undefined;
    
        async function getPagefind() {
          if (pagefind) return pagefind;
          const basePath = import.meta.env.BASE_URL;
          const moduleUrl = `${basePath.replace(/\/$/, '')}/pagefind/pagefind.js`;
          const module = await import(/* @vite-ignore */ moduleUrl);
          pagefind = module.default;
          return pagefind;
        }
    
        input?.addEventListener('input', () => {
          window.clearTimeout(timer);
          timer = window.setTimeout(async () => {
            const query = input.value.trim();
            if (!output || !status) return;
            output.replaceChildren();
            if (!query) {
              status.textContent = 'Search titles and posts by keyword.';
              return;
            }
    
            status.textContent = 'Searchingâ€¦';
            try {
              const search = await getPagefind();
              if (!search) throw new Error('Search index unavailable');
              const response = await search.search(query);
              const results = await Promise.all(response.results.slice(0, 10).map((item) => item.data()));
              status.textContent = results.length ? `${results.length}${response.results.length > 10 ? '+' : ''} results` : 'No matching posts.';
              for (const result of results) {
                const link = document.createElement('a');
                link.href = result.url;
                link.className = 'search-result';
                const title = document.createElement('span');
                title.className = 'search-result-title';
                title.textContent = result.meta.title ?? 'Untitled';
                const excerpt = document.createElement('p');
                excerpt.className = 'search-result-excerpt';
                excerpt.textContent = result.excerpt.replace(/<[^>]*>/g, '');
                link.append(title, excerpt);
                output.append(link);
              }
            } catch {
              status.textContent = 'Search is available after a production build. Try `npm run build`, then preview the site.';
            }
          }, 120);
        });
    
        window.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
          if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === 'k') {
            event.preventDefault();
            input?.focus();
          }
        });
      </script>
    </BaseLayout>

    <header class="site-header">
      <div class="shell header-inner">
        <a class="brand serif" href="/" aria-label="Field Notes home">Field Notes<span>.</span></a>
        <nav aria-label="Main navigation" class="main-nav">
          <a href="/blog">Writing</a>
          <a href="/projects">Projects</a>
          <a href="/links">Links</a>
          <button id="search-toggle" class="nav-search" type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="header-search">Search</button>
          <button id="theme-toggle" class="theme-toggle" type="button" aria-label="Switch to light theme" title="Switch theme">Aa</button>
        </nav>
      </div>
      <section id="header-search" class="header-search" hidden aria-label="Search posts">
        <div class="shell header-search-inner">
          <label class="sr-only" for="header-search-input">Search posts</label>
          <input id="header-search-input" class="search-input" type="search" placeholder="Search posts" autocomplete="off" />
          <p id="header-search-status" class="search-status" role="status" aria-live="polite">Type to search posts.</p>
          <div id="header-search-results" class="header-search-results"></div>
        </div>
      </section>
    </header>
    
    <script>
      const toggle = document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#search-toggle');
      const panel = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#header-search');
      const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('#header-search-input');
      const output = document.querySelector<HTMLDivElement>('#header-search-results');
      const status = document.querySelector<HTMLParagraphElement>('#header-search-status');
      type Pagefind = { search: (query: string) => Promise<{ results: Array<{ data: () => Promise<{ url: string; meta: { title?: string }; excerpt: string }> }> }> };
      let pagefind: Pagefind | undefined;
      let timer: number | undefined;
    
      async function getPagefind() {
        if (pagefind) return pagefind;
        const base = import.meta.env.BASE_URL.replace(/\/$/, '');
        const module = await import(/* @vite-ignore */ `${base}/pagefind/pagefind.js`);
        pagefind = module.default as Pagefind;
        return pagefind;
      }
    
      function openSearch() {
        if (!panel || !toggle) return;
        panel.hidden = false;
        toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
        input?.focus();
      }
    
      function closeSearch() {
        if (!panel || !toggle) return;
        panel.hidden = true;
        toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
        toggle.focus();
      }
    
      toggle?.addEventListener('click', () => {
        if (panel?.hidden) openSearch();
        else closeSearch();
      });
    
      document.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
        const target = event.target;
        if (target instanceof Element && target.closest('[data-open-search]')) {
          event.preventDefault();
          openSearch();
        }
      });
    
      input?.addEventListener('input', () => {
        window.clearTimeout(timer);
        timer = window.setTimeout(async () => {
          const query = input.value.trim();
          if (!output || !status) return;
          output.replaceChildren();
          if (!query) {
            status.textContent = 'Type to search posts.';
            return;
          }
    
          status.textContent = 'Searching...';
          try {
            const index = await getPagefind();
            const response = await index.search(query);
            const results = await Promise.all(response.results.slice(0, 8).map((item) => item.data()));
            status.textContent = results.length ? `${results.length}${response.results.length > 8 ? '+' : ''} results` : 'No matching posts.';
            for (const result of results) {
              const link = document.createElement('a');
              link.href = result.url;
              link.className = 'search-result';
              const title = document.createElement('span');
              title.className = 'search-result-title';
              title.textContent = result.meta.title ?? 'Untitled';
              const excerpt = document.createElement('p');
              excerpt.className = 'search-result-excerpt';
              excerpt.textContent = result.excerpt.replace(/<[^>]*>/g, '');
              link.append(title, excerpt);
              output.append(link);
            }
          } catch {
            status.textContent = 'Search is available after a production build. Run npm run build to create the index.';
          }
        }, 120);
      });
    
      window.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
        if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === 'k') {
          event.preventDefault();
          openSearch();
        } else if (event.key === 'Escape' && panel && !panel.hidden) {
          closeSearch();
        }
      });
    </script>

    import { defineCollection, z } from 'astro:content';
    
    const sharedFields = {
      title: z.string(),
      description: z.string(),
      date: z.coerce.date(),
      draft: z.boolean().default(false),
    };
    
    const posts = defineCollection({
      type: 'content',
      schema: z.object({
        ...sharedFields,
        updated: z.coerce.date().optional(),
        tags: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
        image: z.string().optional(),
      }),
    });
    
    const projects = defineCollection({
      type: 'content',
      schema: z.object({
        ...sharedFields,
        status: z.enum(['active', 'complete', 'archived']).default('complete'),
        url: z.string().url().optional(),
        repository: z.string().url().optional(),
        tags: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
        image: z.string().optional(),
      }),
    });
    
    const links = defineCollection({
      type: 'content',
      schema: z.object({
        ...sharedFields,
        url: z.string().url(),
        source: z.string().optional(),
        tags: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
      }),
    });
    
    export const collections = { posts, projects, links };
    ---
    title: "Welcome to Field Notes"
    description: "Why this small corner of the internet exists, and what I hope to put here."
    date: 2026-09-29
    tags:
      - life
      - craft
    draft: false
    ---
    
    There is something useful about having a place to think in public without having to perform for a feed.
    
    This blog is an ongoing collection of notes about making things with care. Some will be practical. Some will be unfinished. The common thread is attention: to the tools we choose, the systems we build, and the quality of the ordinary decisions in between.
    
    ## A slower publishing rhythm
    
    I want these pages to feel more like a desk drawer than a content machine. A few good notes are enough. If something here helps you make a better decision or notice something you had been rushing past, it has done its job.
    
    Thanks for reading.

    import PostCard from '../components/PostCard.astro';

            </div>
            <p class="mt-10 text-sm leading-6 text-[var(--muted)]">An independent, low-noise corner of the internet. Notes on making, learning, and paying attention.</p>

    import { getPosts, getTagMap, postSlug, formatDate } from '../lib/posts';
    const posts = await getPosts();

        </nav>
      </section>}
    
      {recentPosts.length > 0 && <section>
        <h2 class="sidebar-label">Recent notes</h2>

    import { getCollection } from 'astro:content';
    export async function getPosts(){return (await getCollection('posts',({data})=>!data.draft)).sort((a,b)=>b.data.date.valueOf()-a.data.date.valueOf())}
    export function formatDate(date:Date){return new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en',{dateStyle:'long'}).format(date)}
    export function postSlug(id:string){return id.replace(/\.(md|mdx)$/,'')}
    export function readingTime(body:string){return Math.max(1,Math.ceil(body.trim().split(/\s+/).length/200))}
    export async function getTagMap(){const posts=await getPosts();return posts.reduce<Record<string,typeof posts>>((map,post)=>{post.data.tags.forEach(tag=>(map[tag]??=[]).push(post));return map}, {})}

    type Reference = { title: string; url: string };
    
    export function getPostReferences(body: string, references: Reference[] = []): Reference[] {
      const found = new Map<string, Reference>();
      for (const reference of references) found.set(reference.url, reference);
    
      const inlineLink = /\[([^\]]+)\]\((https?:\/\/[^\s)]+)(?:\s+[^)]*)?\)/g;
      for (const match of body.matchAll(inlineLink)) {
        if (match.index !== undefined && body[match.index - 1] === '!') continue;
        const url = match[2].replace(/[.,;:!?]+$/, '');
        found.set(url, { title: match[1].replace(/[*_`]/g, '').trim(), url });
      }
    
      const bareUrl = /https?:\/\/[^\s<>"')\]]+/g;
      for (const match of body.matchAll(bareUrl)) {
        const url = match[0].replace(/[.,;:!?]+$/, '');
        if (!found.has(url)) found.set(url, { title: url, url });
      }
    
      return [...found.values()];
    }

          <a href="/search" data-open-search>Search posts</a>
        </nav>
      </section>
    
      {tags.length > 0 && <section>
        <h2 class="sidebar-label">Topics</h2>
        <nav class="sidebar-links" aria-label="Topics">
          {tags.map(([tag, taggedPosts]) => <a href={`/tags/${encodeURIComponent(tag)}`}>{tag}<span>{taggedPosts.length}</span></a>)}
        </nav>
      </section>}
    
      {recentPosts.length > 0 && <section>
        <h2 class="sidebar-label">Recent notes</h2>
        <ul class="sidebar-recent">
          {recentPosts.map((post) => <li><a href={`/blog/${postSlug(post.id)}`}>{post.data.title}</a><time datetime={post.data.date.toISOString()}>{formatDate(post.data.date)}</time></li>)}
        </ul>
      </section>}
      </>}
    </aside>
    type Reference = { title: string; url: string };
    
    export function getPostReferences(body: string, references: Reference[] = []): Reference[] {
      const found = new Map<string, Reference>();
      for (const reference of references) found.set(reference.url, reference);
      const prose = body.replace(/```[\s\S]*?```/g, '').replace(/`[^`]*`/g, '');
    
      const inlineLink = /\[([^\]]+)\]\((https?:\/\/[^\s)]+)(?:\s+[^)]*)?\)/g;
      for (const match of prose.matchAll(inlineLink)) {
        if (match.index !== undefined && prose[match.index - 1] === '!') continue;
        const url = match[2].replace(/[.,;:!?]+$/, '');
        found.set(url, { title: match[1].replace(/[*_`]/g, '').trim(), url });
      }
    
      const bareUrl = /https?:\/\/[^\s<>"')\]]+/g;
      for (const match of prose.matchAll(bareUrl)) {
        const url = match[0].replace(/[.,;:!?]+$/, '');
        if (!found.has(url)) found.set(url, { title: url, url });
      }
    
      return [...found.values()];
    }

## Assistant

Post list rows now highlight on hover and keyboard focus. On article pages, the sidebar shows only that post’s tags; a separate “Links in this post” aside lists external Markdown links and bare URLs, excluding code blocks. You can add a `references` list in frontmatter when you want a citation to appear under a clearer title.

I did not run the build or type check for this change.

          <a href="/projects">Projects</a>
          <a href="/links">Links</a>
          <button id="search-toggle" class="nav-search" type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="header-search">Search</button>
          <button id="theme-toggle" class="theme-toggle" type="button" aria-label="Switch to light theme" title="Switch theme">Aa</button>
        </nav>
      </div>
      <section id="header-search" class="header-search" hidden aria-label="Search posts">
        <div class="shell header-search-inner">
          <label class="sr-only" for="header-search-input">Search posts</label>
          <input id="header-search-input" class="search-input" type="search" placeholder="Search posts" autocomplete="off" />
          <p id="header-search-status" class="search-status" role="status" aria-live="polite">Type to search posts.</p>
          <div id="header-search-results" class="header-search-results"></div>
        </div>
      </section>
    </header>
    
    <script>
      const toggle = document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#search-toggle');
      const panel = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#header-search');
      const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('#header-search-input');
      const output = document.querySelector<HTMLDivElement>('#header-search-results');
      const status = document.querySelector<HTMLParagraphElement>('#header-search-status');
      type Pagefind = { search: (query: string) => Promise<{ results: Array<{ data: () => Promise<{ url: string; meta: { title?: string }; excerpt: string }> }> }> };
      let pagefind: Pagefind | undefined;
      let timer: number | undefined;
    
      async function getPagefind() {
        if (pagefind) return pagefind;
        const base = import.meta.env.BASE_URL.replace(/\/$/, '');
        const module = await import(/* @vite-ignore */ `${base}/pagefind/pagefind.js`);
        pagefind = module.default as Pagefind;
        return pagefind;
      }
    
      function openSearch() {
        if (!panel || !toggle) return;
        panel.hidden = false;
        toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
        input?.focus();
      }
    
      function closeSearch() {
        if (!panel || !toggle) return;
        panel.hidden = true;
        toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
        toggle.focus();
      }
    
      toggle?.addEventListener('click', () => {
        if (panel?.hidden) openSearch();
        else closeSearch();
      });
    
      document.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
        const target = event.target;
        if (target instanceof Element && target.closest('[data-open-search]')) {
          event.preventDefault();
          openSearch();
        }
      });
    
      input?.addEventListener('input', () => {
        window.clearTimeout(timer);
        timer = window.setTimeout(async () => {
          const query = input.value.trim();
          if (!output || !status) return;
          output.replaceChildren();
          if (!query) {
            status.textContent = 'Type to search posts.';
            return;
          }
    
          status.textContent = 'Searching...';
          try {
            const index = await getPagefind();
            const response = await index.search(query);
            const results = await Promise.all(response.results.slice(0, 8).map((item) => item.data()));
            status.textContent = results.length ? `${results.length}${response.results.length > 8 ? '+' : ''} results` : 'No matching posts.';
            for (const result of results) {
              const link = document.createElement('a');
              link.href = result.url;
              link.className = 'search-result';
              const title = document.createElement('span');
              title.className = 'search-result-title';
              title.textContent = result.meta.title ?? 'Untitled';
              const excerpt = document.createElement('p');
              excerpt.className = 'search-result-excerpt';
              excerpt.textContent = result.excerpt.replace(/<[^>]*>/g, '');
              link.append(title, excerpt);
              output.append(link);
            }
          } catch {
            status.textContent = 'Search is available after a production build. Run npm run build to create the index.';
          }
        }, 120);
      });
    
      window.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
        if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === 'k') {
          event.preventDefault();
          openSearch();
        } else if (event.key === 'Escape' && panel && !panel.hidden) {
          closeSearch();
        }
      });
    </script>

    ---
    title: "Welcome to Field Notes"
    description: "Why this small corner of the internet exists, and what I hope to put here."
    date: 2026-09-29
    tags:
      - life
      - craft
    draft: false
    ---
    
    There is something useful about having a place to think in public without having to perform for a feed.
    
    This blog is an ongoing collection of notes about making things with care. Some will be practical. Some will be unfinished. The common thread is attention: to the tools we choose, the systems we build, and the quality of the ordinary decisions in between.
    
    ## A slower publishing rhythm
    
    I want these pages to feel more like a desk drawer than a content machine. A few good notes are enough. If something here helps you make a better decision or notice something you had been rushing past, it has done its job.
    
    Thanks for reading.

    {references.length > 0 && <aside class="post-references" aria-label="Links and references mentioned in this post">
      <h2 class="sidebar-label">Links in this post</h2>
      <ul class="sidebar-references">
        {references.map((reference: { title: string; url: string }) => <li><a href={reference.url} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">{reference.title}</a></li>)}
      </ul>
    </aside>}
    type Reference = { title: string; url: string };
    
    export function getPostReferences(body: string, references: Reference[] = []): Reference[] {
      const found = new Map<string, Reference>();
      for (const reference of references) found.set(reference.url, reference);
      const prose = body.replace(/```[\s\S]*?```/g, '').replace(/`[^`]*`/g, '');
    
      const inlineLink = /\[([^\]]+)\]\((https?:\/\/[^\s)]+)(?:\s+[^)]*)?\)/g;
      for (const match of prose.matchAll(inlineLink)) {
        if (match.index !== undefined && prose[match.index - 1] === '!') continue;
        const url = match[2].replace(/[.,;:!?]+$/, '');
        if (!found.has(url)) found.set(url, { title: match[1].replace(/[*_`]/g, '').trim(), url });
      }
    
      const bareUrl = /https?:\/\/[^\s<>"')\]]+/g;
      for (const match of prose.matchAll(bareUrl)) {
        const url = match[0].replace(/[.,;:!?]+$/, '');
        if (!found.has(url)) found.set(url, { title: url, url });
      }
    
      return [...found.values()];
    }

A document assistant can start with Workers and AI Search; use Vectorize and Workers AI when it needs custom retrieval. Recommend only the pieces the requested behavior needs.
    
    ## Find guidance for a task not listed here
    
    Use the [Cloudflare product directory](https://developers.cloudflare.com/directory/) for additional products and their current docs. Follow links to the specific feature or API involved. Use [Choose a data or storage product](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/storage-options/) for storage tradeoffs, and the product's limits, pricing, and migration guides when evaluating scale, cost, or an upgrade. This table maps common tasks to selected Cloudflare products; it does not enumerate every possible application.
    
    ## Caching
    
    Prefer [Workers Cache](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/) for caching, including [advanced patterns](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/examples/) using cached inner entrypoints and programmatic invalidation. Choose [Cache API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/cache/) or KV caching only when a concrete requirement cannot be met by Workers Cache; check its [patterns](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/examples/) and [limitations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/limitations/) first.
    
    ## Working principles
    
    - Inspect the existing project and its pinned package versions before choosing an API or configuration shape.
    - Retrieve current Cloudflare documentation when details may have changed. Use installed types and `node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json` when they represent the project's pinned version.
    - Preserve the project's architecture and make the smallest change that satisfies the request.
    - Check current Cloudflare docs before relying on limits, prices, compatibility flags, or security requirements; these can change.
    - Validate in proportion to the change: use the project's checks, then exercise the affected behavior when practical.

    ---
    name: wrangler
    description: Run or troubleshoot Wrangler CLI commands and configure Worker projects for local development, deployment, and Cloudflare resource management.
    ---
    
    # Wrangler CLI
    
    Use the project's Wrangler version and retrieve the relevant documentation before writing commands or configuration. CLI flags and configuration fields change; do not rely on memorized examples.
    
    ## Inspect the Project
    
    - Find the package manager, installed Wrangler version, package scripts, framework, and Wrangler config. Run commands through the project's scripts or package manager so they use its local version. Install dependencies using the existing lockfile when needed; do not silently upgrade Wrangler to match current docs. If Wrangler is not a dependency, follow the [installation guide](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/install-and-update/) to add it locally.
    - Identify the config used by the build or deploy command, including framework-generated config. Edit its source rather than generated output.
    - Establish the target account, Worker, environment, and resource before running commands that change them. For data operations, determine whether the target is local or remote.
    
    ## Retrieve What the Task Needs
    
    Use the Cloudflare MCP `docs` tool if available, or fetch the relevant linked page directly. Follow links to the specific command or product involved; avoid loading the entire reference. If a page moves, rediscover it through the [Wrangler command index](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/commands/) or Cloudflare docs search.
    
    | Task | Source |
    | --- | --- |
    | Discover commands and flags, including resource management, deployments, rollback, and diagnostics | Project-local `wrangler --help` and `wrangler <command> --help`; [command reference](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/commands/) |
    | Edit config or add a binding | Installed `wrangler/config-schema.json` (usually under `node_modules`); [configuration reference](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/) |
    | Deploy a framework application | [Framework guides](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/framework-guides/); follow the guide for the project's existing framework and adapter |
    | Migrate an application to Workers when requested | [Pages to Workers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/migration-guides/migrate-from-pages/); [Vercel to Workers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/migration-guides/vercel-to-workers/) |
    | Configure staging or production | [Environments](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/environments/) |
    | Set secrets locally, in CI, or on a deployed Worker | [Secrets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/secrets/) |
    | Generate binding and runtime types | [TypeScript](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/languages/typescript/) |
    | Run locally or choose a testing approach | [Local development](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/local-development/); [testing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/testing/) |
    | Diagnose authentication or select an account | [General commands](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/commands/general/), including `whoami`; [authentication profiles](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/profiles/) |
    | Deploy an unauthenticated prototype | [Claim deployments](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/claim-deployments/) for eligibility, expiry, and claim URL handling; use a permanent account for production or CI |
    
    Use installed help and schema to check whether documented features exist in the project's version. If a required feature needs an upgrade, make that dependency explicit. If retrieval is unavailable, state the gap and use available local evidence rather than inventing syntax.
    
    ## Apply the Change
    
    - Prefer `wrangler.jsonc` for new config. Set a new project's [compatibility date](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/compatibility-dates/) to today; review runtime changes and test when advancing an existing project's date. Preserve existing project conventions and avoid incidental format migrations.
    - Check environment inheritance before adding bindings or variables. Some fields must be specified separately for each environment; a working default config does not establish that staging is configured.
    - With the Cloudflare Vite plugin, select the environment via `CLOUDFLARE_ENV` at dev or build time. Deploy the resulting build; setting an environment at deploy time does not retarget its flattened config. See [Vite environments](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/vite-plugin/reference/cloudflare-environments/).
    - Reconcile dashboard changes with the config before deploying: Wrangler can overwrite dashboard variables and routes. When binding existing resources, verify their identifiers; omitted identifiers can trigger [automatic provisioning](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/#automatic-provisioning).
    - Distinguish local simulation from remote bindings during development. A locally running Worker can still access real resources; check the selected bindings before testing writes.
    - Keep secret values out of command arguments, source code, and logs. Use the documented interactive input or protected file/stdin mechanism for the command. Local secret files must be ignored by version control and are not automatically uploaded as deployed secrets. For missing local secrets, check file precedence and any `secrets.required` declaration in the secrets docs.
    - Treat `wrangler secret put` and `secret delete` as deployments: they create a version and deploy it immediately. Use the documented `wrangler versions secret` workflow when the change must be staged.
    - Before a rollback, check [rollback limitations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/versions-and-deployments/rollbacks/): connected resources and their data are not rolled back with Worker code.
    
    ## Validate
    
    After changing config or bindings in a TypeScript project, regenerate types with the project's `wrangler types` command rather than hand-editing generated declarations. Run the relevant existing typecheck or tests.
    
    For deployment changes, use the project's build workflow and `wrangler deploy --dry-run` where supported, with the intended config and environment. A successful dry run checks the build and packaging; it does not prove remote resources or runtime behavior work. Use task-specific local or remote checks as appropriate to the requested work.
    
    Report what changed, the target environment, checks performed, and any unresolved validation gaps. Link the documentation used when the result depends on current command or configuration behavior.
